common_mistake: Fe'l bo'lganda 'slip up' ajratib yoziladi; 'slip-up' shakli faqat ot (xatolik) sifatida qo'llaniladi.

definition_en: to be mainly decided or explained by one thing
example_en: Success often comes down to consistent practice.
example_uz: Muvaffaqiyat ko'pincha muntazam mashq qilishga bog'liq bo'ladi.

definition_en: to take further action about something
example_en: I will follow up on your application tomorrow.
example_uz: Ertaga arizangiz bo'yicha keyingi ishlarni tekshiraman.

definition_en: to begin or deal with a task in a particular way
example_en: She explained how to go about solving the problem.
example_uz: U muammoni yechishga qanday kirishishni tushuntirdi.

definition_en: to study a subject by reading about it
example_en: I read up on the company before my interview.
example_uz: Suhbatdan oldin kompaniya haqida batafsil o'rganib chiqdim.

definition_en: to start working or studying hard
example_en: We need to knuckle down before the final exam.
example_uz: Yakuniy imtihondan oldin o'qishga jiddiy kirishishimiz kerak.

definition_en: to watch carefully for someone or something
example_en: Look out for an email confirming your booking.
example_uz: Broningizni tasdiqlovchi xatni kuzatib turing.

definition_en: to suggest an idea or plan for consideration
example_en: The committee put forward a practical solution.
example_uz: Qo'mita amaliy yechimni ilgari surdi.

definition_en: to reserve time or money for a purpose
example_en: Set aside an hour each day for vocabulary practice.
example_uz: Har kuni lug'at mashqi uchun bir soat ajratib qo'ying.

definition_en: to separate something into its component parts
example_en: The technician took the device apart to repair it.
example_uz: Texnik qurilmani ta'mirlash uchun qismlarga ajratdi.

definition_en: to start doing something with determination
example_en: They set about improving the course immediately.
example_uz: Ular darhol kursni yaxshilashga kirishdilar.

definition_en: to gradually develop a feeling or ability
example_en: He worked up the confidence to speak in public.
example_uz: U omma oldida gapirish uchun asta-sekin ishonch hosil qildi.

definition_en: to prepare a complete written version of notes or research
example_en: Please write up the results in a formal report.
example_uz: Natijalarni rasmiy hisobot shaklida to'liq yozib chiqing.

definition_en: Used when you want to start a process, meeting, or project.
example_en: Let's get the ball rolling on this marketing project immediately.
example_uz: Keling, bu marketing loyihasini darhol boshlab yuboraylik.
word_family: get the ball rolling on | help get the ball rolling
common_mistake: Saying 'make the ball rolling'

translation_uz: Qisqa bog'lanib hol-ahvol so'rashmoq yoki yangilik almashmoq
translation_ru: Чтобы ненадолго связаться, чтобы спросить, как дела или обменяться новостями.
definition_en: Used when you want to reconnect with someone to check on their status or get an update.
example_en: I'll touch base with you later this week to see how the report is coming along.
example_uz: Hisobot qanday ketayotganini bilish uchun hafta oxirida siz bilan qisqacha bog'lanaman.
word_family: touch base with | touch base on | briefly touch base | need to touch base
common_mistake: Saying 'touch the base'

definition_en: Used when you want to ensure you are kept informed about ongoing developments or changes.
example_en: Please keep me in the loop regarding the progress of the negotiations.
example_uz: Muzokaralar qanday ketayotgani haqida meni xabardor qilib turing.
word_family: keep someone in the loop | stay in the loop | fully in the loop
common_mistake: Saying 'stay in the circle'

definition_en: Used to describe the most important fact or the final result of a situation.
example_en: The bottom line is that we need to increase our sales to survive.
example_uz: Xulosa shuki, omon qolish uchun savdolarimizni oshirishimiz kerak.
word_family: the bottom line is that | affect the bottom line | improve the bottom line
common_mistake: Using it to refer to a literal line at the bottom of a page

translation_uz: Bir xil tushunishga kelmoq, fikrlari bir joydan chiqmoq
translation_ru: Прийти к тому же пониманию, выйти из того же места
definition_en: Used when two or more people have reached a common understanding or agreement on a topic.
example_en: I just want to make sure we are all on the same page before we launch.
example_uz: Ishni boshlashdan oldin hammamiz bir xil tushunayotganimizga ishonch hosil qilmoqchiman.
word_family: ensure everyone is on the same page | confirm we are on the same page
common_mistake: on the same book

translation_uz: Har ikki tomon uchun foydali bo'lgan vaziyat
definition_en: Used to describe a scenario where every party involved benefits.
example_en: This partnership is a win-win situation for both our companies.
example_uz: Bu hamkorlik ikkala kompaniyamiz uchun ham foydali vaziyatdir.
word_family: create a win-win situation | lead to a win-win situation
common_mistake: Saying 'win-win scenario' (redundant)

definition_en: Encouraging creative or unconventional ideas when solving a problem.
example_en: To compete in this market, we really need to think outside the box.
example_uz: Bu bozorda raqobatlashish uchun haqiqatan ham noodatiy fikrlashimiz kerak.
word_family: encouraged to think outside the box | forced to think outside the box
common_mistake: Thinking outside of the box (less common)

headword: at the end of the day
definition_en: Used to summarize the most important point after considering all facts.
example_en: At the end of the day, our priority must be customer satisfaction.
example_uz: Oxir-oqibat, bizning ustuvor vazifamiz mijozlar mamnunligi bo'lishi kerak.
word_family: ultimately | priority | bottom line | fact | decide
common_mistake: at the end of day (missing 'the')

definition_en: Used to complain about someone changing the rules or requirements of a task after it has already started.
example_en: It is frustrating when the client keeps moving the goalposts on this project.
example_uz: Mijoz bu loyihada shartlarni doim o'zgartiraversa, juda asabiylasharli.
word_family: constantly moving | moving the goalposts on | keep moving | frustrating
common_mistake: moving the goals

definition_en: Used when describing what value, skills, or ideas a person or company contributes to a collaboration.
example_en: She brings over ten years of experience to the table.
example_uz: U hamkorlikka o'n yildan ortiq tajriba olib keladi.
word_family: what you bring to the table | bring something valuable to the table
common_mistake: bring on the table (wrong preposition)

definition_en: Used to describe actions that create a noticeable, measurable impact on results.
example_en: We need a strategy that actually moves the needle on our annual sales growth.
example_uz: Yillik savdo o'sishimizga sezilarli ta'sir qiladigan strategiya kerak.
synonyms: make an impact | show results | affect the outcome
word_family: really move the needle | move the needle significantly
common_mistake: move the needles

definition_en: Used when evaluating whether a project, task, or meeting provides enough value to justify the time spent.
example_en: Is it worth my while to attend the conference in London?
example_uz: Londondagi konferensiyaga borish vaqtimga arziydimi?
word_family: make it worth my while | ensure it is worth my while | hardly worth my while
common_mistake: Worth my time

translation_uz: Murakkab o'rganish jarayoni, ko'p narsani tez o'rganish kerak bo'lgan vaziyat
translation_ru: Сложный процесс обучения, ситуация, когда многим вещам нужно научиться быстро.
definition_en: Used when describing a task or job that is difficult to learn because it is complex or requires new skills.
example_en: Using this new software comes with a rather steep learning curve.
example_uz: Ushbu yangi dasturdan foydalanish ancha murakkab o'rganish jarayonini talab qiladi.
word_family: very steep learning curve | face a steep learning curve
common_mistake: A high learning curve

definition_en: Used to describe someone who is feeling sad, depressed, or lacking energy for a period of time.
example_en: He has been a bit down in the dumps since he lost his job.
example_uz: Ishini yo'qotganidan beri uning ruhi biroz tushib yuribdi.
word_family: a bit down in the dumps | feeling down in the dumps | stay down in the dumps
common_mistake: using 'in the dump' (singular)

definition_en: Used when someone is extremely angry or outraged, often showing it through their behavior.
example_en: The passengers were fuming because the flight was delayed by six hours.
example_uz: Parvoz olti soatga kechiktirilgani uchun yo'lovchilar juda jahli chiqdi.
word_family: absolutely fuming | fuming about | fuming at | fuming with rage
common_mistake: saying 'fuming at someone' without a reason

headword: to be at one's wits' end
translation_uz: nima qilishni bilmay qolgan, asabi charchagan
translation_ru: он не знал, что делать, он был измотан
definition_en: Used when someone has tried everything to solve a problem and is now completely frustrated or anxious.
example_en: I’ve tried fixing the computer three times; I’m at my wits' end.
example_uz: Kompyuterni uch marta tuzatishga urindim; endi nima qilishni bilmay qoldim.
word_family: completely at my wits' end | drove me to my wits' end | at my wits' end with
common_mistake: using 'at my wit end'

definition_en: Used when someone is nervous, tense, or anxious about something that might happen.
example_en: I've been on edge all day waiting for the exam results.
example_uz: Imtihon natijalarini kutib, kun bo'yi tarang edim.
word_family: feel on edge | keep someone on edge | remain on edge | appear on edge
common_mistake: in edge

translation_ru: быть удивленным или сбитым с толку
definition_en: Used when someone is surprised or shocked by something unexpected, often in a way that leaves them momentarily speechless.
example_en: I was quite taken aback by his blunt response.
example_uz: Uning keskin javobidan ancha hayron qoldim.
word_family: completely taken aback | taken aback by | utterly taken aback
common_mistake: taken back

headword: to be at the end of one's tether
definition_en: Used when you have run out of patience or energy to deal with a difficult situation.
example_en: I'm at the end of my tether with this noisy neighbour.
example_uz: Shu shovqinchi qo'shnidan sabrim butunlay tugadi.
word_family: reach the end of one's tether | be at the end of one's tether
common_mistake: saying 'at the end of the rope' (which is the American version, but 'tether' is more common in UK)

definition_en: Used when someone is deeply affected or hurt by criticism or a negative event.
example_en: Don't take his comments to heart; he’s just having a bad day.
example_uz: Uning gaplarini yuragingizga yaqin olmang; uning shunchaki kuni yomon o'tyapti.
word_family: take criticism to heart | really take it to heart | not take it to heart
common_mistake: saying 'take to the heart'

headword: to get a kick out of
definition_en: Used to express that you find something fun, exciting, or highly enjoyable.
example_en: I really get a kick out of learning new languages.
example_uz: Yangi tillarni o'rganish menga juda zavq bag'ishlaydi.
word_family: get a real kick out of | get a huge kick out of | get a kick out of watching
common_mistake: saying 'get a kick in'

headword: to be sick and tired of
translation_uz: juda charchagan bo'lmoq (biron narsadan to'yib ketmoq)
definition_en: Expressing deep annoyance or frustration with a situation that has persisted for too long.
example_en: I'm sick and tired of hearing the same excuses every day.

definition_en: Used when you are confused, overwhelmed by too much information, or experiencing vertigo.
example_en: There's so much information in this module that my head is spinning.
example_uz: Bu modulda shuncha ko'p ma'lumot borki, boshim aylanib ketdi.
word_family: head is spinning from | leave my head spinning | make my head spin
common_mistake: saying 'my head is turning'

definition_en: Used when you are annoyed or bored because a situation has continued for too long.
example_en: I'm fed up with this constant rainy weather.
example_uz: Bu tinimsiz yomg'irli ob-havodan to'yib ketdim.
word_family: getting fed up with | thoroughly fed up with | pretty fed up with
common_mistake: Saying 'I fed up'

translation_ru: продолжить работу, начать как можно скорее
definition_en: Used to say you are starting a task or continuing with a task energetically.
example_en: We've got a lot to finish, so let's crack on.
example_uz: Tugatishimiz kerak bo'lgan ish ko'p, keling, ishni davom ettiraylik.
synonyms: get down to | proceed | carry on
word_family: crack on with work | time to crack on | let's crack on | crack on immediately
common_mistake: thinking it means to break something

definition_en: Used when you think someone is teasing you or telling you a lie for fun.
example_en: Wait, did you really win the lottery, or are you just pulling my leg?
example_uz: To'xtang, lotereyada rostdan ham yutdingizmi yoki meni hazillashib aldayapsizmi?
word_family: only pulling my leg | just pulling my leg | stop pulling my leg
common_mistake: Saying 'pull my arm'

translation_uz: o'zini yo'qotib qo'ymoq, aqldan ozmoq, vaziyatni boshqara olmaslik
translation_ru: потерять себя, потерять рассудок, оказаться не в состоянии контролировать ситуацию
definition_en: Used when someone starts acting strangely, becomes angry, or loses their ability to behave logically or calmly.
example_en: He completely lost the plot when he found out the train was cancelled.
example_uz: Poezd bekor qilinganini bilib, u butunlay o'zini yo'qotib qo'ydi.
word_family: totally lost the plot | nearly lost the plot | completely lost the plot
common_mistake: Saying 'lost my plot' instead of 'lost the plot'

definition_en: British slang for leaving a place quickly, often to avoid paying for something or to avoid an unpleasant situation.
example_en: The kids did a runner as soon as they saw the teacher coming.
example_uz: Bolalar o'qituvchi kelayotganini ko'rishi bilan qochib ketishdi.
word_family: try to do a runner | did a runner from | threaten to do a runner
common_mistake: Saying 'do the runner'

definition_en: Used when leaving a place briefly to go somewhere close, like a shop or a neighbour's house.
example_en: I’m just going to pop out to the shops for some milk.
example_uz: Men sut olish uchun do'konga qisqa muddatga chiqib kelaman.
synonyms: nip out | step out | run an errand
word_family: pop out for a bit | pop out to the shops | pop out for lunch | just popping out
common_mistake: saying 'I pop out to work' (implies you are leaving forever/not coming back soon)

definition_en: Used to show that you accept an excuse or a point of view, even if it is not what you initially wanted.
example_en: I can't go to the cinema tonight because I'm broke. - Fair enough.
example_uz: Bugun kechqurun kinoga bora olmayman, chunki pulim yo'q. — Tushunarli.
word_family: that's fair enough | fair enough, I suppose | fair enough, but...
common_mistake: It is fair enough (usually used as an interjection)

definition_en: A very British way of saying you are pleased or proud about something.
example_en: I was really chuffed with my exam results.
example_uz: Imtihon natijalarimdan juda xursand bo'ldim.
word_family: chuffed to bits | well chuffed | chuffed with results | really chuffed
common_mistake: Chuffed for something (it is 'chuffed with')

definition_en: Idiomatic way to describe heavy rainfall.
example_en: I forgot my umbrella and it's been raining buckets since I left the house.
example_uz: Soyabonimni unutdim va uyimdan chiqqanimdan beri chelaklab yomg'ir yog'yapti.
word_family: Raining buckets | Been raining buckets | Forecast to rain buckets
common_mistake: Saying 'buckets of water'

headword: to be a bit of a nightmare
definition_en: Used to describe a situation, journey, or task that is frustrating, difficult, or chaotic.
example_en: The traffic on the motorway was a bit of a nightmare this morning.
example_uz: Bugun ertalab avtomagistraldagi tirbandlik ancha muammoli edi.
antonyms: a breeze | a piece of cake
word_family: a total nightmare | a bit of a nightmare | find it a nightmare
common_mistake: saying 'the nightmare' instead of 'a nightmare'

definition_en: Used in British English to suggest an activity or ask if someone wants to do something.
example_en: Do you fancy grabbing a pizza later tonight?
example_uz: Bugun kechqurun pizza yeyishga qanday qaraysiz?
word_family: fancy a coffee | fancy a bite | fancy a walk | really fancy | not fancy
common_mistake: do you fancy to go (must be V-ing)

translation_uz: esimdan chiqib ketdi, kallam ishlamay qoldi
translation_ru: Я забыл, мой разум перестал работать
definition_en: Used when you are under pressure (like an exam or presentation) and suddenly cannot remember information.
example_en: I walked into the exam, and suddenly my mind went blank.
example_uz: Imtihon xonasiga kirganimda, birdaniga esimdan hamma narsa chiqib ketdi.
word_family: suddenly went blank | totally went blank | panic made my mind go blank
common_mistake: my brain became empty (unnatural)

translation_ru: посоветоваться с кем-то / узнать его мнение
definition_en: Used when you want to show someone an idea or plan to see if they approve or have feedback.
example_en: I have an idea for the presentation, can I run it by you?
example_uz: Taqdimot uchun bir fikrim bor, uni siz bilan maslahatlashsam bo'ladimi?
word_family: run an idea by someone | run a plan by someone | run something by a colleague
common_mistake: Run to someone

headword: a bit of a long shot
definition_en: Used when describing something that is unlikely to succeed or happen.
example_en: Asking for a promotion right now is a bit of a long shot.
example_uz: Hozir lavozim oshirishni so'rash unchalik ham real bo'lmagan umid.
antonyms: a sure thing | a dead cert
word_family: considered a long shot | definitely a long shot | worth a long shot
common_mistake: It is a long distance

definition_en: Used to describe being away from home, usually doing chores, running errands, or simply socialising in public.
example_en: I've been out and about all day, so I'm absolutely exhausted.
example_uz: Kun bo'yi ko'chada yuribman, shuning uchun juda holdan toyganman.
word_family: been out and about | while out and about | all out and about
common_mistake: I am out and in (incorrect idiom)

definition_en: Used when you are struggling to reach a decision and finally do so.
example_en: I still haven't made up my mind about which university to apply to.
example_uz: Qaysi universitetga hujjat topshirish haqida hali qaror qabul qilmaganman.
antonyms: be undecided | be on the fence | waver
word_family: finally make up one's mind | hard to make up one's mind
common_mistake: Decide my mind (incorrect verb usage)

headword: to make a point of doing something
translation_uz: atayin biror narsa qilmoq / shuni odat qilmoq
translation_ru: делать что-то намеренно / сделать это привычкой
definition_en: Used when you deliberately ensure you do something because you think it is important.
example_en: I make a point of reading for an hour every night.
example_uz: Har oqshom bir soat kitob o'qishni odat qilganman.
word_family: make a point of saying | make a point of visiting | make a point of calling
common_mistake: make a point to do

definition_en: A polite and standard way to offer or ask for help.
example_en: Could you give me a hand with these heavy boxes?
example_uz: Shu og'ir qutilarni ko'tarishga menga yordam bera olasizmi?
word_family: gladly give a hand | need a hand | give a hand with | give a quick hand
common_mistake: Give a hand to him (word order is awkward)

translation_uz: biror nima qilmoqchi bo'lmoq / nima qilib yuribsan?
definition_en: Used to ask what someone is doing or to describe someone's current activities/intentions.
example_en: What have you been up to lately?
example_uz: So'nggi paytlarda nimalar bilan band bo'lib yuribsiz?
word_family: up to no good | up to something | what are you up to | been up to
common_mistake: What are you up to do? (incorrect structure)

definition_en: Use this to politely admit that you forgot to do something or forgot an appointment.
example_en: I am so sorry, it completely slipped my mind to pay the bill.
example_uz: Uzr, hisobni to'lash butunlay esimdan chiqib ketibdi.
word_family: completely slipped my mind | had slipped my mind | it briefly slipped my mind
common_mistake: It slipped out of my mind (incorrect idiom)

definition_en: Use this to say that someone's guess, opinion, or performance is exactly right.
example_en: Your assessment of the situation was spot on.
example_uz: Vaziyat haqidagi bahoingiz juda aniq edi.
word_family: completely spot on | absolutely spot on | spot on the money
common_mistake: Your answer is very spot on (don't use intensifiers like 'very' as it is already emphatic)

definition_en: Used when someone decides to try a new activity or task, often despite being uncertain about the outcome.
example_en: I've never played tennis before, but I'm willing to give it a go.
example_uz: Avval tennis o'ynamaganman, lekin uni sinab ko'rishga tayyorman.
word_family: give it a good go | worth a go | give something a quick go | might give it a go
common_mistake: Give a go it (wrong word order)

definition_en: Used to express interest or willingness to participate in a suggested plan or activity.
example_en: Are you up for going out tonight?
example_uz: Bugun kechqurun tashqariga chiqishga tayyormisiz?
word_family: definitely up for | not up for | up for anything | up for a laugh
common_mistake: I am up to go to the cinema (incorrect preposition)

definition_en: A very British way to express frustration or annoyance about something recurring.
example_en: This constant rain is really doing my head in.
example_uz: Bu tinimsiz yomg'ir rosa asabimga tegayapti.
word_family: really doing my head in | starts to do my head in | does my head in completely
common_mistake: Changing the pronoun (e.g., 'it does head in me')

headword: to make a go of it
translation_uz: urinib ko'rmoq / muvaffaqiyatga erishishga harakat qilmoq
definition_en: Used when someone decides to try their best to make a venture, relationship, or situation successful.
example_en: They decided to open a cafe and really make a go of it.
example_uz: Ular kafe ochishga va uni muvaffaqiyatli yuritishga jiddiy harakat qilishga qaror qildilar.
word_family: make a real go of it | trying to make a go of it | determined to make a go of it
common_mistake: Using 'make to go of it'

headword: i'm tied up at the moment
translation_ru: Я сейчас занят/у меня нет времени
definition_en: Used when you cannot deal with someone or a task immediately because you are busy with something else.
example_en: I'm tied up at the moment, can I call you back in an hour?
example_uz: Hozir bandman, bir soatdan keyin sizga qayta qo'ng'iroq qilsam bo'ladimi?
antonyms: free | available | at a loose end
word_family: thoroughly tied up | a bit tied up | tied up with work | tied up in a meeting
common_mistake: I am tie up now

definition_en: A friendly, casual way to say goodbye to friends or colleagues.
example_en: I have to run to class now, catch you later!
example_uz: Hozir darsga yugurishim kerak, keyin ko'rishamiz!
word_family: catch you later on | catch you later then | just catch you later
common_mistake: Catch you after

translation_ru: Мне это не интересно/он мне не очень нравится
definition_en: A polite and common way to state that you do not like a specific activity or hobby.
example_en: Do you want to go to the jazz concert? Honestly, I'm not really into it.
example_uz: Jazz konsertiga borishni xohlaysizmi? Rostini aytsam, menga unchalik yoqmaydi.
antonyms: I'm keen on it | I'm a big fan of it | I'm into it
word_family: not really into that | not really into heavy metal | not really into sports
common_mistake: I am not in it

definition_en: A standard, welcoming phrase used when someone visits your house or workspace.
example_en: Come in! Make yourself at home while I put the kettle on.
example_uz: Kiring! Choynakni qo'yib kelgunimcha, o'zingizni uyingizdagidek his qiling.
word_family: truly make yourself at home | feel free to make yourself at home
common_mistake: Make yourself in home

definition_en: Used to confirm that something is logical, reasonable, or easy to understand.
example_en: That makes sense; I never thought of it that way.
example_uz: Bu mantiqli ekan; men bu haqda hech qachon bunday o'ylamagan edim.
word_family: it makes perfect sense | it makes complete sense | doesn't make any sense
common_mistake: it is sense (wrong construction)

definition_en: Used when giving a rough estimate rather than an exact, precise number.
example_en: I don't know the exact cost, but could you give me a ballpark figure?
example_uz: Aniq narxni bilmayman, lekin taxminiy hisobni ayta olasizmi?
word_family: give a ballpark figure | provide a ballpark figure | a rough ballpark figure
common_mistake: Ballpark number (less natural than 'figure')

translation_uz: dam olmoq / o'zingni qiynama / xotirjam bo'l
definition_en: Used to tell someone to relax or not to worry, or as a way of saying goodbye.
example_en: You've been working too hard; you really need to take it easy this weekend.
example_uz: Juda ko'p ishlayapsiz; bu dam olish kunlari albatta biroz dam olishingiz kerak.
word_family: take it easy on someone | need to take it easy | advice to take it easy
common_mistake: Take it easily (incorrect adverb usage)

definition_en: Used when you are ready to leave a place or a social gathering.
example_en: It's getting late, I think it's time for me to make a move.
example_uz: Kech bo'lib qoldi, menimcha, ketishim kerak.
word_family: time to make a move | really make a move | need to make a move
common_mistake: I'm going to make a movement (incorrect vocabulary)

definition_en: Used when you are considering different choices before making a final decision.
example_en: I need a few days to weigh up my options before accepting the job offer.
example_uz: Ish taklifini qabul qilishdan oldin variantlarimni yaxshilab o'ylab ko'rish uchun bir necha kun kerak.
word_family: carefully weigh up | weigh up the pros and cons | need to weigh up
common_mistake: I am weighing to the options (wrong verb usage)

definition_en: Used when students stay awake all night to study or finish an assignment before a deadline.
example_en: I had to pull an all-nighter to finish my final dissertation before the deadline.
example_uz: Muddatdan oldin yakuniy dissertatsiyamni tugatish uchun butun kecha uxlamasdan ishlashimga to'g'ri keldi.
synonyms: to burn the midnight oil | to stay up all night
word_family: frequently pull an all-nighter | exhausting all-nighter | studying session
common_mistake: do an all-nighter

definition_en: Used to describe completing a task or an exam very easily and successfully.
example_en: Because she had studied so hard, she managed to breeze through the final exam.
example_uz: U juda ko'p tayyorlangani uchun yakuniy imtihondan qiynalmay o'tdi.
word_family: breeze through effortlessly | breeze through easily | breeze through the paper
common_mistake: breeze the exam

definition_en: Used when someone passes a test or succeeds, but only just, usually by a very small margin.
example_en: I didn't prepare well enough, so I only managed to scrape through the maths exam.
example_uz: Yetarlicha tayyorlanmagandim, shuning uchun matematika imtihonidan zo'rg'a o'tdim.
antonyms: pass with flying colours | breeze through
word_family: scrape through an exam | scrape through a test | barely scrape through
common_mistake: to scrape passed

definition_en: Used to describe passing an exam or finishing a course with little to no effort.
example_en: She studied so hard that she managed to sail through her final examinations.
example_uz: U juda ko'p o'qigani uchun yakuniy imtihonlardan osonlikcha o'tdi.
word_family: sail through exams | sail through an assessment | sail through an interview
common_mistake: sail into the exam

definition_en: Used when starting to understand a complicated subject or a new method of study.
example_en: It took me a while to get to grips with the new research methodology.
example_uz: Yangi tadqiqot metodologiyasini tushunib olishimga biroz vaqt ketdi.
word_family: get to grips with basics | get to grips with a problem
common_mistake: get grips to

definition_en: Used when someone achieves an excellent score or succeeds in a challenge with high merit.
example_en: She was nervous about the physics paper, but she passed with flying colours.
example_uz: U fizika imtihonidan xavotirda edi, lekin uni a'lo natija bilan topshirdi.
word_family: passed with flying colours | graduated with flying colours
common_mistake: pass with flying color

definition_en: Used when discussing who should pay for environmental cleanups or climate change mitigation.
example_en: Governments should foot the bill for transitioning to renewable energy.
example_uz: Hukumatlar qayta tiklanadigan energiyaga o'tish xarajatlarini qoplashi kerak.
synonyms: pay for | finance | cover the costs
word_family: foot the bill for climate change | foot the bill for pollution
common_mistake: foot the cost

definition_en: Used to describe the negative, gradual damage caused by pollution or human activity.
example_en: Industrial waste is taking a heavy toll on our marine life.
example_uz: Sanoat chiqindilari dengiz hayotimizga juda katta zarar yetkazmoqda.
word_family: take a heavy toll | take a toll on biodiversity | take a toll on the environment
common_mistake: take a toll to

definition_en: Used when describing species or ecosystems in critical danger of disappearing.
example_en: Many species are currently on the brink of extinction due to habitat loss.
example_uz: Ko'plab turlar yashash joylari yo'qolishi sababli hozir yo'q bo'lib ketish yoqasida.
synonyms: on the verge of | approaching | near
word_family: on the brink of extinction | on the brink of collapse | on the brink of disaster
common_mistake: on the edge to

headword: to be at a tipping point
definition_en: Used to describe a critical moment where a system is about to change irreversibly, often used in climate change discussions.
example_en: Many scientists argue that our planet is at a tipping point regarding global warming.
example_uz: Ko'plab olimlar sayyoramiz global isish masalasida hal qiluvchi nuqtada turganini ta'kidlaydi.
word_family: critical tipping point | reach a tipping point | climate tipping point
common_mistake: saying 'in a tipping point'

definition_en: Used to describe modern cultures that prioritize disposable items over repairs or recycling.
example_en: We need to move away from a throwaway society if we want to save resources.
example_uz: Resurslarni saqlamoqchi bo'lsak, ishlatib tashlash madaniyatidan voz kechishimiz kerak.
word_family: combat a throwaway society | the rise of a throwaway society
common_mistake: Using 'throwable society'.

headword: to be on the brink of disaster
definition_en: Used when describing an ecosystem or the planet nearing a point of irreversible environmental damage.
example_en: Many scientists warn that our oceans are on the brink of disaster.
example_uz: Ko'plab olimlar okeanlarimiz halokat yoqasida ekanidan ogohlantirmoqda.
synonyms: at the point of no return | teetering on the edge
word_family: on the brink of collapse | on the brink of extinction | on the brink of disaster
common_mistake: Saying 'on the edge of disaster' (less common colocation).

definition_en: Used to describe severe negative consequences of an action on the environment or health.
example_en: Industrial pollution has taken a heavy toll on the river's ecosystem.
example_uz: Sanoat ifloslanishi daryo ekotizimiga juda katta zarar yetkazdi.
synonyms: devastate | severely affect | wreak havoc on
word_family: pollution | ecosystem | marine life | biodiversity | decades
common_mistake: saying 'take a heavy damage on'

definition_en: Used in academic or news contexts to describe species, habitats, or ecosystems under severe threat.
example_en: Many endangered species are currently in jeopardy due to rapid deforestation.
example_uz: Ko'plab yo'qolib borayotgan turlar tezkor o'rmon kesilishi tufayli xavf ostida.
synonyms: at stake | under threat | in peril
word_family: ecosystem in jeopardy | future in jeopardy | put in jeopardy
common_mistake: saying 'in the jeopardy'

definition_en: Used when describing a major shift in a situation from negative to positive, often regarding environmental change.
example_en: International climate agreements might finally turn the tide on global warming.
example_uz: Xalqaro iqlim bitimlari nihoyat global isish vaziyatini ijobiy tomonga burishi mumkin.
synonyms: reverse the situation | change the outcome
antonyms: worsen the situation | fail to make an impact
word_family: turn the tide against | turn the tide on | effectively turn the tide
common_mistake: using 'change the tide'

headword: to put a strain on nature
definition_en: Used to describe how human activity causes stress or damage to natural ecosystems.
example_en: Rapid urbanisation is putting a huge strain on nature and local wildlife.
example_uz: Tez urbanizatsiya tabiat va mahalliy yovvoyi hayvonotga katta bosim o'tkazmoqda.
antonyms: relieve the pressure | ease the burden
word_family: put a strain on resources | put a strain on ecosystems | severe strain
common_mistake: using 'make a strain' instead of 'put a strain'

headword: foot the bill for environmental damage
translation_uz: ekologik zararlar uchun to'lovni amalga oshirish
definition_en: Used in discussions about who should pay for cleanup or ecological repairs, often used in policy or academic debates.
example_en: The government insists that major polluters must foot the bill for the environmental damage they cause.
example_uz: Hukumat yirik ifloslantiruvchilar yetkazgan ekologik zarar uchun xarajatlarni qoplashi shartligini ta'kidlamoqda.
synonyms: pay for | cover the costs | shoulder the expenses
word_family: corporate polluters | legal requirement | costly cleanup | long-term restoration
common_mistake: footing the bill of

definition_en: Used when describing something valuable that risks being lost or destroyed, such as the future of the planet.
example_en: The future of the Amazon rainforest is at stake.
example_uz: Amazon o'rmonlarining kelajagi xavf ostida.
synonyms: in danger | at risk | in jeopardy
word_family: lives are at stake | future is at stake | everything is at stake | much at stake
common_mistake: saying 'the future is on stake'

headword: to be at the mercy of nature
definition_en: Used to express the helplessness of humans when facing extreme weather or natural disasters.
example_en: When a hurricane hits, islanders are entirely at the mercy of nature.
example_uz: Dovul urganda, orol aholisi butunlay tabiat injiqliklariga bog'liq bo'ladi.
word_family: entirely | constantly | forces | elements
common_mistake: in the mercy of

definition_en: Used to describe the severe damage or destruction caused by natural disasters or pollution.
example_en: Plastic pollution continues to wreak havoc on marine ecosystems.
example_uz: Plastik ifloslanish dengiz ekotizimlariga katta talafot yetkazishda davom etmoqda.
word_family: wreak havoc on the environment | wreak havoc on local communities
common_mistake: saying 'wreak the havoc on'

definition_en: Used to describe who or what suffers the most severe impact from a negative event like climate change or pollution.
example_en: Developing nations often bear the brunt of climate change.
example_uz: Rivojlanayotgan davlatlar ko'pincha iqlim o'zgarishining asosiy zarbasini o'z zimmasiga oladi.
synonyms: suffer the most | take the full force of
word_family: bear the brunt of climate change | bear the brunt of pollution
common_mistake: Using 'take' instead of 'bear'

definition_en: Used to describe making a small but important personal contribution to a larger environmental effort.
example_en: I try to do my bit for the environment by recycling plastic.
example_uz: Men plastikni qayta ishlash orqali atrof-muhit uchun o'z hissamni qo'shishga harakat qilaman.
synonyms: contribute | play one's part | chip in
word_family: everyone do their bit | try to do one's bit | urge citizens to do their bit
common_mistake: Do my piece

definition_en: Used when talking about reconnecting with the environment or living a more natural, simplified life.
example_en: Many people move to the countryside to get back to nature.
example_uz: Ko'p odamlar tabiatga yaqinlashish uchun qishloqqa ko'chib o'tadi.
synonyms: reconnect with nature | immerse in nature
word_family: desire to get back to nature | opportunity to get back to nature
common_mistake: Go back to nature

translation_uz: Bu oson tanlov (o'ylab o'tirishga ham hojat yo'q)
translation_ru: Это простой выбор (вам даже не придется об этом думать)
definition_en: Used to suggest that a decision is so obvious or beneficial that it requires very little thinking.
example_en: Choosing to study at that university was a no-brainer for me.
example_uz: O'sha universitetda o'qishni tanlash men uchun oson qaror edi.
word_family: absolute no-brainer | total no-brainer | pretty much a no-brainer
common_mistake: It is a no brainer

translation_uz: Buning hech qanday zarari yo'q (qilib ko'rish kerak)
translation_ru: В этом нет никакого вреда (надо попробовать)
definition_en: Used to encourage someone to try something new or take a small risk.
example_en: There's no harm in checking the official website for more details.
example_uz: Rasmiy veb-saytni batafsilroq ma'lumot uchun tekshirib ko'rishning zarari yo'q.
synonyms: It's worth trying | Give it a go
antonyms: It's a bad idea | Avoid doing
word_family: harm in trying | harm in asking | harm in checking | harm in applying
common_mistake: There is no harm to try

headword: leaves a lot to be desired
definition_en: Used to express that something is unsatisfactory or of poor quality without being overly aggressive.
example_en: The public transport system in this town leaves a lot to be desired.
example_uz: Bu shahardagi jamoat transporti tizimi talab darajasida emas.
word_family: the quality leaves a lot to be desired | really leaves a lot to be desired
common_mistake: It leaves many to be desired.

definition_en: Used when something sounds too good to be true and there is a hidden problem or condition.
example_en: The offer seems amazing, but I'm sure there's a catch.
example_uz: Taklif juda zo'r ko'rinadi, lekin unda biror yashirin shart borligiga ishonaman.
word_family: I suspect there's a catch | the catch is that | what's the catch?
common_mistake: There is a trap.

headword: it comes with its fair share of problems
translation_ru: У него есть свой набор проблем
definition_en: Used to acknowledge that while something has benefits, it also has a predictable amount of issues.
example_en: Living in a big city comes with its fair share of problems.
example_uz: Katta shaharda yashashning o'ziga yarasha muammolari bor.
synonyms: it has its drawbacks | it is not without issues | it faces challenges
antonyms: it is completely straightforward | it is seamless
word_family: fair share of problems | fair share of challenges | fair share of difficulties
common_mistake: It comes with fair share of problem

translation_ru: Одним из недостатков является то, что / является одной из ловушек.
definition_en: Used when discussing hidden dangers or common mistakes people fall into while doing something.
example_en: One of the pitfalls of starting a business is underestimating the costs.
example_uz: Biznes boshlashdagi xatarlardan biri xarajatlarni past baholashdir.
synonyms: One of the risks is | One of the dangers is
word_family: avoid common pitfalls | a major pitfall | potential pitfalls
common_mistake: One of the pitfall is...

definition_en: Used when discussing a specific problem that makes progress difficult or prevents achieving a goal.
example_en: Funding remains a significant hurdle for small startups nowadays.
example_uz: Hozirgi kunda mablag' kichik startaplar uchun katta to'siq bo'lib qolmoqda.
antonyms: A great opportunity | A major boost
word_family: Face a significant hurdle | Overcome a significant hurdle
common_mistake: A significant hurdle to do...

definition_en: Used when something fails to meet an expected standard or requirement.
example_en: The new proposal falls short of the safety standards required by law.
example_uz: Yangi taklif qonun talab qiladigan xavfsizlik standartlariga yetmaydi.
synonyms: underperform | fail to reach | be deficient
antonyms: exceed expectations | meet the standard | surpass
word_family: fall short of expectations | fall short of the target
common_mistake: Saying 'it falls short expectation' (missing 'of')

definition_en: Used to introduce an opposing or negative perspective after discussing a positive one.
example_en: Working from home is convenient, but the flip side is feeling isolated.
example_uz: Uydan ishlash qulay, ammo buning ikkinchi tomoni — o'zingizni yolg'iz his qilishdir.
synonyms: the other side of the coin | the converse | the downside
word_family: consider the flip side | the flip side of | the dark flip side
common_mistake: Flip side of that is...

translation_uz: Umuman yoqimsiz narsa / qiziqishni so'ndiradigan narsa
translation_ru: Что-то вообще неприятное/что-то, что отключает интерес
definition_en: Used to describe something that makes you lose interest or dislike a situation/product.
example_en: The high price of the tickets was a real turn-off for the fans.
example_uz: Chipta narxining yuqoriligi muxlislar uchun juda yoqimsiz omil bo'ldi.
antonyms: a major draw | an attractive feature
word_family: real turn-off | major turn-off | total turn-off
common_mistake: It is a turning-off...

definition_en: Used to acknowledge that something has benefits, but still faces specific challenges.
example_en: Digital learning is great, but it's not without its problems.
example_uz: Raqamli ta'lim zo'r, ammo uning ham o'z muammolari bor.
synonyms: It has flaws | It faces challenges
word_family: certainly not without its problems | hardly without its problems
common_mistake: It is not without problem.

headword: a real thorn in my side
definition_en: Used to describe a persistent, ongoing problem that is very annoying and difficult to ignore.
example_en: The lack of parking space has been a real thorn in my side for months.
example_uz: To'xtash joyining yetishmasligi bir necha oydan beri mening doimiy muammom bo'lib kelmoqda.
synonyms: A major headache | A persistent bother
antonyms: A breath of fresh air | A great help
word_family: become a real thorn | constant thorn | a thorn in the side of | remain a thorn
common_mistake: A thorn in my body.

definition_en: Used when something is annoying, frustrating, or inconvenient, but not a life-changing disaster.
example_en: Waiting for the bus in the rain is a bit of a pain.
example_uz: Yomg'irda avtobus kutish biroz noqulaylik.
antonyms: a breeze | a piece of cake
word_family: real pain | a bit of a pain | total pain | to be a pain in the neck
common_mistake: Using it to describe serious issues (e.g., poverty)

headword: it's a bit of a let-down
definition_en: Used when something is disappointing because it didn't meet expectations or had a hidden flaw.
example_en: The movie had great reviews, but the ending was a bit of a let-down.
example_uz: Film haqida yaxshi fikrlar bo'lsa ham, uning yakuni biroz ko'ngilni qoldirdi.
word_family: major let-down | bit of a let-down | complete let-down | felt like a let-down
common_mistake: It's a let-down of...

definition_en: Used to describe a small, unexpected problem or complication that might stop progress.
example_en: We have the funding, but the only snag is finding the right location.
example_uz: Bizda mablag' bor, ammo yagona muammo — to'g'ri joy topish.
word_family: hit a snag | minor snag | potential snag | the only snag
common_mistake: The only snag is that it is a big problem

headword: there is a price to pay
definition_en: Used when describing the negative consequences or sacrifices required for a specific outcome.
example_en: Success is great, but there is always a price to pay for it.
example_uz: Muvaffaqiyat zo'r, lekin uning uchun har doim ma'lum bir badal to'lash kerak.
synonyms: There are trade-offs | It involves sacrifices
word_family: a heavy price to pay | a steep price to pay | a high price to pay
common_mistake: There is a price to pay of

definition_en: Used to introduce negative aspects of something that is otherwise generally seen as good or popular.
example_en: The electric vehicle is an excellent invention, but it is not without its faults.
example_uz: Elektr avtomobili ajoyib ixtiro, ammo u kamchiliklardan xoli emas.
synonyms: It has a few flaws | It is imperfect
antonyms: It is flawless | It is perfect
word_family: certainly not without its faults | admittedly not without its faults
common_mistake: It is not without faults it.

definition_en: Used to introduce a contrasting point or perspective, typically after presenting an initial argument.
example_en: Renewable energy is cheaper long-term; on the other hand, the initial investment is very high.
example_uz: Qayta tiklanadigan energiya uzoq muddatda arzonroq; boshqa tomondan, boshlang'ich sarmoya juda katta.
antonyms: Similarly | Likewise | In the same vein
word_family: to present a different view | to balance the argument | a counterpoint
common_mistake: Using 'on another hand' instead of the correct phrase.

definition_en: Used to concede a point or introduce a contrasting observation that slightly contradicts or moderates what was just stated.
example_en: The new software is incredibly complex. Having said that, the training provided is excellent.
example_uz: Yangi dastur juda murakkab. Shuni aytgan bo'lsam ham, berilgan trening a'lo.
synonyms: That said | Nevertheless | All the same
word_family: to introduce a caveat | to acknowledge a drawback | to soften a criticism
common_mistake: Using 'have said that' or incorrect tense.

definition_en: Used to acknowledge a fact or argument as true, but then to state that it does not change the main point or conclusion.
example_en: The budget for the project is indeed tight. Be that as it may, we are expected to deliver the same high-quality results.
example_uz: Loyiha byudjeti, albatta, tor. Shunday bo'lsa-da, bizdan o'sha yuqori sifatli natijalarni yetkazish kutiladi.
word_family: to concede a point | to acknowledge an objection | the fact remains
common_mistake: Using it in informal speech where 'anyway' or 'still' would be more natural.

definition_en: Used to introduce a point that logically follows from the previous one, applying the same principle or reasoning to a different situation.
example_en: If we reward innovation, we must accept some failed experiments. By the same token, punishing all failure stifles creativity.
example_uz: Agar innovatsiyani rag'batlantirsak, ayrim muvaffaqiyatsiz tajribalarni ham qabul qilishimiz kerak. Xuddi shu sababga ko'ra, har bir muvaffaqiyatsizlikni jazolash ijodkorlikni bo'g'adi.
synonyms: For the same reason | Similarly | In like manner
word_family: the logic applies | the principle holds | it follows that
common_mistake: Using it as a simple synonym for 'similarly' without the logical connection.

definition_en: Used to introduce a statement that contrasts with or outweighs all the points previously mentioned, often expressing a surprising or significant conclusion.
example_en: The film had a weak script, mediocre acting, and poor pacing. For all that, it was a huge commercial success.
example_uz: Filmning ssenariysi zaif, aktyorligi o'rtacha va tempi sust edi. Shunga qaramay, u katta tijorat muvaffaqiyatiga erishdi.
synonyms: Despite all this | Nevertheless | Even so
word_family: to acknowledge shortcomings | a surprising outcome | a redeeming feature
common_mistake: Using it simply to mean 'because of all that' (causal) instead of its concessive (contrasting) meaning.

definition_en: Used when adding an extra, usually stronger, point to a previous argument or fact.
example_en: The hotel was overpriced. On top of that, the service was terrible.
example_uz: Mehmonxona qimmat edi. Buning ustiga, xizmati ham yomon edi.
word_family: On top of that, it is | On top of that, there is | On top of that, she is
common_mistake: Using 'On top of that' to contrast instead of add

definition_en: Used to express that something is generally true, though there might be exceptions.
example_en: The students were, for the most part, well-behaved during the lecture.
example_uz: Talabalar, asosan, ma'ruza paytida o'zlarini yaxshi tutishdi.
word_family: For the most part, they | For the most part, it is | For the most part, people
common_mistake: Saying 'in the most part'

translation_uz: ...dan tubdan farq qiladi / ...ga qaraganda butunlay boshqacha
definition_en: Used to express that something is very different from what it used to be or what was expected.
example_en: This modern office is a far cry from the cramped space we had before.
example_uz: Bu zamonaviy ofis avvalgi tor joyimizdan mutlaqo farq qiladi.
word_family: A far cry from reality | A far cry from perfection | A far cry from ideal
common_mistake: It is far cry from

definition_en: Used to say that two things are of the same quality or standard.
example_en: The salary offered is on a par with industry standards for this role.
example_uz: Taklif etilgan maosh ushbu lavozim uchun soha standartlari bilan bir xil darajada.
word_family: roughly on a par with | largely on a par with | clearly on a par with
common_mistake: On par with

definition_en: Used to emphasise that something is totally different from or not as good as something else.
example_en: The final movie was nothing like the book I read.
example_uz: Yakuniy film men o'qigan kitobga umuman o'xshamadi.
synonyms: Completely different from | A far cry from
word_family: nothing like as good | nothing like as fast | look nothing like
common_mistake: Not nothing like

definition_en: Used to introduce an alternative, often negative, aspect of a topic you have just discussed.
example_en: Living in London is exciting; on the flip side, it is incredibly expensive.
example_uz: Londonda yashash qiziqarli; boshqa tomondan, u nihoyatda qimmat.
word_family: The flip side is that | Look at the flip side | Consider the flip side
common_mistake: Using 'On the flip side of'

definition_en: Used when two things are not exactly identical but share very similar characteristics.
example_en: Both models are much the same in terms of performance.
example_uz: Ikkala model ham ishlashi jihatidan deyarli bir xil.
word_family: Pretty much the same | Remain much the same | Look much the same
common_mistake: Using 'much same' without 'the'

definition_en: Used to strongly emphasise that something is much less adjective than something else. Very high-frequency in spoken IELTS to show natural range.
example_en: The sequel to the movie was nowhere near as good as the original.
example_uz: Filmning davomi asl nusxadek yaxshi emas edi.
synonyms: not nearly as | not nearly so | far inferior to
word_family: nowhere near as good as | nowhere near as expensive as
common_mistake: nowhere near than

definition_en: Used when placing two things together to easily observe differences or similarities.
example_en: When you look at the photos side by side, the difference is obvious.
example_uz: Suratlarni yonma-yon ko'rsangiz, farq yaqqol bilinadi.
synonyms: next to each other | in tandem
word_family: work side by side | compare side by side | place side by side
common_mistake: Saying 'side to side' (this usually means moving left to right)

definition_en: A highly effective transition to start a comparison or focus on a specific topic.
example_en: When it comes to sports, he is an expert.
example_uz: Sport haqida gap ketganda, u mutaxassis.
word_family: When it comes to technology | When it comes to the crunch
common_mistake: When come to

definition_en: Used to describe something that has a very positive effect on a problem or situation.
example_en: A quick walk in the morning can work wonders for your mood.
example_uz: Ertalabki qisqa sayr kayfiyatingizga juda yaxshi ta'sir qilishi mumkin.
word_family: Work wonders for | Work wonders on | Truly work wonders
common_mistake: It works a wonder

definition_en: Used to describe something that is useful or helpful in specific, practical situations.
example_en: A good laptop really comes in handy when you're a student.
example_uz: Talaba bo'lganingizda yaxshi noutbuk juda qo'l keladi.
synonyms: is very useful | is quite practical | is beneficial
antonyms: is useless | is a waste of time
word_family: comes in handy for | comes in handy when | comes in handy later
common_mistake: It comes in a handy

definition_en: Used to acknowledge that something has good points, often used when admitting something is not perfect but still has benefits.
example_en: Living in a big city has its perks, like better nightlife.
example_uz: Katta shaharda yashashning, masalan, tungi hayot yaxshiroq bo'lishi kabi, o'z afzalliklari bor.
synonyms: has its advantages | has its upsides
word_family: certainly has its perks | definitely has its perks | has its fair share of perks
common_mistake: It has perks

headword: there's a lot to be said for
translation_uz: X ning ko'plab ijobiy tomonlari bor
definition_en: Used to express that something has significant advantages, especially when others might doubt it.
example_en: There's a lot to be said for taking a gap year before starting university.
example_uz: Universitetni boshlashdan oldin bir yil tanaffus qilishning ko'plab ijobiy tomonlari bor.
synonyms: Has a lot of merits | Is highly beneficial
antonyms: There is little to be said for
word_family: a lot to be said for | much to be said for | something to be said for
common_mistake: There is much to be said of...

definition_en: Used when an advantage provides a competitive superiority in a specific area.
example_en: Learning a second language gives you the edge in the job market.
example_uz: Ikkinchi tilni o'rganish sizga mehnat bozorida ustunlik beradi.
synonyms: provides a competitive advantage | gives a leg up
word_family: give you the edge | the competitive edge | gain the edge
common_mistake: gives you an edge over to

headword: brings a lot to the table
definition_en: Used when describing the positive qualities or advantages someone or something contributes to a team or project.
example_en: She brings a lot to the table with her ten years of experience in marketing.
example_uz: U marketing sohasidagi o'n yillik tajribasi bilan jamoaga katta qiymat qo'shadi.
synonyms: to be beneficial | to be an asset | contributes value
antonyms: doesn't add much value | is redundant
word_family: brings a lot to the table | what does it bring to the table
common_mistake: brings much to the table

definition_en: Used to describe an advantage that is undeniable, obvious, and easy to identify.
example_en: A clear-cut benefit of moving to the city is the access to better transport.
example_uz: Shaharga ko'chishning yaqqol afzalligi — yaxshi transportga kirish imkonidir.
antonyms: A hidden disadvantage | A marginal benefit
word_family: clear-cut benefit | clear-cut advantage | clear-cut result | clear-cut winner
common_mistake: A clear-cut of benefit

headword: it gives you a head start
translation_uz: Bu senga ustunlik beradi (yoki yutuqli boshlanish)
definition_en: Used to describe an advantage gained by starting earlier or having something others don't have.
example_en: Learning a language as a child gives you a head start in school.
example_uz: Bolalikda til o'rganish maktabda sizga yaxshi boshlang'ich ustunlik beradi.
word_family: give a head start | get a head start | have a head start | major head start
common_mistake: It gives a head start to me

definition_en: Used to describe a factor or situation that gives someone an advantage or improves their chances of success.
example_en: Having previous work experience really works in your favour during interviews.
example_uz: Oldingi ish tajribasiga ega bo'lish suhbatlarda sizning foydangizga ishlaydi.
synonyms: To one's advantage | Beneficial to someone
word_family: work in one's favour | tilt in one's favour | tip in one's favour
common_mistake: It works for my favour
